recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-31943 unless FHIR-I later changes the GET/POST search support model or asks for additional implementation-note examples beyond the existing sensitive-link and state-tracking guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-31943 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked to remove or relax mandatory POST search support, but the final decision retained core GET and POST search support, added 405 Method Not Allowed leeway when a method cannot process a specific search, disallowed failing both methods, and requested method-choice, security, example, and paging-link clarifications.
initial_application: No historical source-changing commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-31943 was found. Same-family R5 commits applied the substance: a8509373541feb0c553e8c86dfe2bdf0136efee7 added GET/POST plus 405 conformance language, 7415a1eb0824ba59d977db335205d71eed004312 added POST examples, f47290bddbd45abf5ead98478c1796e50bb8ea83 added 405 search guidance, and e441170220c19e992f803667b245e63dcdd508cf moved HTTP-specific method guidance to source/http.html.
additional_context: The linked #implementers Zulip thread shows the ambiguity that led to the tracker: implementers debated mandatory GET/POST support, IG constraints, POST security assumptions, and self/paging links. FHIR-I minutes record the 2021-10-18 vote and 2021-10-25 follow-up on sensitive paging links. Related reconciliation commits for FHIR-31944, FHIR-38994, FHIR-39137, FHIR-35859, FHIR-36126, and FHIR-46649 are already on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source was changed. source/http.html already states the GET/POST support and 405 rule, includes GET and POST examples, and contains method-choice, security, and testing guidance. source/search.html already requires self/paging links to be GET-style and warns against sensitive paging URL content except for self links; source/http.html also documents GET follow-up paging and state-tracking parameters.
